commit.message:
ssh/tailssh: route SSH forwarding through the privileged monitor

Route tailssh's forwarding through the per-connection ssh-monitor, so
on unix forwarded sockets are dialed and bound by children with the
authenticated local user's credentials, never by root tailscaled.

- unix -L, direct-streamlocal: the lexical allowlist check stays in
  tailscaled as coarse policy. The allowlist is home, /tmp, and
  /run/user/<uid>. Relative and abstract paths are rejected. The dial
  then runs as the user through the monitor. The EvalSymlinks
  re-validation is dropped, and the kernel's DAC is the boundary. The
  allowlist is capped. A home directory that cleans to "/" or is empty
  would prefix-match every absolute path, and such an entry is dropped
  instead. Paths at or beyond the sun_path capacity reject lexically
  rather than dying at bind or dial with a generic EINVAL.
- unix -R, streamlocal-forward: the listener is created by a user-cred
  child with umask-at-bind 0600 and unlink-if-owned. Closing it does
  not unlink the socket, and the stale file on cancel is accepted.
- TCP -R, tcpip-forward: a tailssh-owned handler replaces gliderssh's
  ForwardedTCPHandler. The bind goes through the monitor's listen op
  with the local user's credentials, so privileged ports fail by
  kernel construction for non-root-mapped users. Root-mapped users are
  allowed, as in OpenSSH. Bind addresses are loopback-only unless
  TS_SSH_FORWARD_GATEWAY_PORTS is set, the equivalent of sshd's
  GatewayPorts.
- agent forwarding: the socket and its containing directory are
  created by a user-cred child, a 0600 socket in a 0700 user-owned
  directory, instead of a root-run MkdirTemp, Chmod, and Chown
  sequence. Session-end cleanup is unchanged.

The monitor is spawned lazily on the first forwarding or agent need,
from the tailscaled binary, and closed when the SSH connection ends.
closeFwdMonitor latches a closed flag under the fwd lock, so a caller
racing the teardown is refused by fwdMonitor, or reads the current
state without spawning through fwdMonitorIfAny, instead of respawning
a monitor nobody ever closes.

plan9 keeps today's behavior through a build-tagged seam, fwdmonitor.go
and fwdplan9.go. There is no monitor on plan9. Unix forwarding is
rejected there, and reverse TCP forwarding keeps the gliderssh
handler with the mayReversePortForwardTo gate.

Tests cover conn-level callbacks against a real monitor and real
one-shot fwd children: allowlist rejections, user-owned 0600 sockets, a
foreign sticky-dir socket not unlinked, loopback, gateway-ports, and
privileged-port TCP binds, agent directory hygiene and cleanup, and
TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING coverage, plus refused respawn after
teardown. The unix-fwd root-dial regressions cover a static
in-allowlist symlink to a root-owned 0600 canary, which must fail
permission denied as the bound user, and a dir-swap race, which must
never serve the protected canary.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: add user-credential forwarding children and monitor dial/listen ops

Add the one-shot "be-child ssh-fwd" children that perform forwarded
socket work, and the monitor and client plumbing for the socket ops.
The conn and session flows do not use the ops yet. The next commit
routes them.

- fwdchild.go: a child re-execed by the monitor, born unprivileged at
  clone. The monitor applies the connection's bound identity as
  SysProcAttr.Credential, so the kernel's DAC sees the connection
  user's permissions. It dials a unix socket, or creates one with
  umask-at-bind mode and optional unlink-if-owned, or binds a TCP
  listener, or creates the agent-forwarding socket in a user-owned
  directory. The result returns to the monitor over an inherited
  socketpair as one status line with at most one descriptor attached.
- monitor.go: handleDial and handleListen run the ops on one-shot
  children with a spawn-to-result deadline, monFwdOpDeadline. On
  expiry the child's group is SIGKILLed. killChild reaps such a child
  with a bounded non-blocking wait. A child left in uninterruptible
  sleep is abandoned in its own group rather than blocking the loop
  goroutine. The dial and listen placeholder replies are gone, and
  their not-implemented test with them.
- monitor_client.go: Dial, Listen, and ListenAgent over the existing
  request-ID plumbing.
- incubator.go, monitor_linux.go, monitor_other.go: registration and
  per-platform spawn attributes for the fwd children.

Tests drive real children across uid boundaries. They cover dial and
bind round trips, unix and TCP listens, agent-listen directory
hygiene, unlink-if-owned, peer-credential assertions, and the
no-identity-keys-on-the-wire shape of every request.

Forwarding children spawn with an empty environment through
spawnRPCChild: they take everything from argv and the result socket,
and the daemon's environment must not reach a child running as the
connection's user.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: add monitor RPC codec and SCM_RIGHTS fd passing

New self-contained code for the per-connection privileged ssh-monitor.
No existing behavior or wiring changes. Later commits wire the
forwarding and session paths onto it.

rpcFrame is the newline-delimited JSON wire struct with request IDs.
It covers dial, listen, exec, signal, and ping requests, ok and err
replies, and unsolicited exit notifications. rpcConn is the framing
codec over one socketpair end. Reads go only through ReadMsgUnix with
a CmsgSpace(3*sizeof(int)) OOB buffer. A plain Read or an undersized
buffer silently drops ancillary data, and the kernel closes the dropped
descriptors. A stream read never returns data beyond an
SCM_RIGHTS-carrying message, so a descriptor arrives with the first
chunk of a split line and survives reassembly. Writes attach
descriptors to the first byte of a line and never to an empty payload.
A short write resends the remainder as plain data, because resending
the ancillary data would duplicate the descriptors. Received
descriptors are marked close-on-exec at parse time, by the codec rather
than by the stdlib's platform-dependent handling. Herald attribution
validates a whole read's herald batch before queueing any set for a
frame, so a failed batch closes its sets exactly once and never
double-closes a set already queued for a frame. Lines are capped at
256 KiB, and NUL bytes and frames carrying more descriptors than their
op declares are rejected on receive. A read timeout returns
os.ErrDeadlineExceeded and preserves any partially received line, so
the monitor's poll loop can sweep between reads without losing the
frame. A read timeout is the only error that preserves state. Every
other error closes all held descriptors and clears the buffer.

sendFds, recvFds, and wrapUnixConn are shared by the monitor and client
sides. wrapUnixConn consumes its fd, because os.NewFile's finalizer
cannot be neutralized from outside.

Tests exercise ping and fd round-trips with liveness and FD_CLOEXEC
checks, multi-fd frames, kernel framing pins for first-chunk ancillary
delivery and undersized-OOB MSG_CTRUNC rejection, 64 KiB-plus
split-line reassembly under a shrunken SO_SNDBUF, oversized and NUL
rejection, the short-write resend path, the read-timeout
state-preservation contract, and 50-way multiplexed request/reply
traffic.

The monitor scrubs every descriptor from 3 up to close-on-exec at
entry and again before each exec. Go's exec closes nothing beyond the
descriptors it passes, so a single non-close-on-exec fd anywhere in the
spawner's table would otherwise reach every child the monitor execs.
close_range(CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC) does the sweep in one syscall on
kernels 5.11+; older kernels scan the self-fd directory. A new test
injects a non-close-on-exec pipe at spawn and pins the clean-child
contract.

spawnRPCChild takes the child's environment explicitly: a nil env
gives the child an empty environment, never the spawner's. The monitor
child is spawned with the daemon's environment; user-identity children
are spawned with none, so the daemon's environment never reaches a
child running as the connection's user.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

tsnet: authorize ListenSSH peers, fix PTY emulation and session queue bound

ListenSSH now documents its session trust model and takes an
authorization callback. A session is accepted from any peer that the
tailnet ACL's TCP rules allow and that resolves with WhoIs. The server
performs no SSH client authentication, does not map the peer to a local
user, and does not record the session. The application is responsible
for what each session does. Set Server.SSHAuthCallback to reject
unwanted sessions before they reach Accept. A rejected session is
refused at open with exit status 1 and is never yielded to Accept. The
callback is plumbed through LocalBackend.ListenSSH and HookListenSSH.
With no callback, behavior is unchanged.

The listener's SSH server runs session channels only, with no port
forwarding. Closing the listener closes the accepted connections.

- DisablePTYEmulation runs on every session, so a PTY session passes
  data through unchanged instead of translating "\n" to "\r\n". The
  translation corrupted binary data read through the net.Conn
  interface. Window changes are drained for every session, even when
  the application never calls Pty, because gliderssh writes window
  changes from the session request loop and an undrained channel
  blocks the session's requests. Pty drops window changes when the
  application is not reading them.

- The handshake is bounded by TS_SSH_LOGIN_GRACE_TIME, default 120
  seconds, the same as sshd's LoginGraceTime.

- TS_SSH_IDLE_TIMEOUT bounds connections with no SSH traffic. It is 0
  by default, and zero applies no bound, so quiet but live sessions
  are not closed by default. Both timeout knobs accept a Go duration
  such as "90s" or a bare number of seconds.

- Accepted sessions wait for Accept in a bounded queue. When the queue
  is full, further sessions are refused, so an application that stops
  calling Accept parks only a bounded number of sessions.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: drain the sftp test helper's stderr copier

sftpSubsystemSession waited for the stdout copier's done channel but not
the stderr copier's. The stderr copier carries the recording-policy
refusal notices. The deferred channel close could cut it off mid-drain.
The refusal text never reached the test's buffer. Both copiers are
now waited on before the channel closes.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: record sftp sessions and honor recording failure policy

Remove the blanket sftp-subsystem exemption from session recording:
in a recording-mandatory tailnet, sftp sessions (and scp -s, which
rides the sftp subsystem) now go through recording setup with the same
OnRecordingFailure semantics — an unreachable recorder refuses the
session (exit 254) instead of letting file access proceed silently
unrecorded.

SFTP casts are metadata-only: the CastHeader identifies the peer, local
user, connection, and records Command = "sftp" (subsystem requests
carry no command string), but no I/O events are captured — the SFTP
wire protocol is binary, so pass-through capture would not be
human-meaningful and would balloon cast sizes. The upload/cleanup
lifecycle is unchanged. With no recorders configured, sftp is
unchanged.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: unify defaultPathForUser to use isRootUser (#21928)

This change unifies all root checks in `ssh/tailssh` to use `isRootUser`. This ensures we consistently avoid the `== "0"` check and protects us in any future root check changes (previously missed in #21919).

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

commit.message:
ssh/tailssh: fix off-by-one and clamp c2n SSH username hint cap

The add closure used len(res.Usernames) > max, letting one extra
username through the client's Max, and the client-supplied Max was used
unclamped. Honor Max exactly and clamp it to a 100-username ceiling;
the list is only a login hint.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: validate accepted env values, deny GLIBC_TUNABLES, cap names

GLIBC_TUNABLES is parsed by glibc in root su/login environments with
AT_SECURE=0 (CVE-2023-4911 class); add it to the dangerous-env-var
denylist next to its GCONV_PATH/LOCPATH siblings.

The TERM/LANG/LC_* pairs accepted without policy (OpenSSH's default
AcceptEnv) had unvalidated values that reach root-exec'd login/su
environments, where glibc treats path-like locale names as locale-data
paths and leading dashes as its own options. Reject path- and
option-like values (and NUL, which would truncate on exec) instead of
trying to sanitize them.

Also cap accepted env var names at 256 bytes before any wildcard
matching, bounding the matcher input and the child's "su -w" allowlist;
real names are short (LOGIN_NAME_MAX).

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: refuse direct-exec fallback for non-root users as root

When tailscaledPath is empty, newIncubatorCommand runs the session's
shell directly, with no be-child incubator to drop privileges. A root
tailscaled could therefore run a non-root user's session as root.
Refuse that case, mirroring canSwitchToLocalUser's semantics.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: hand the agent forwarding dir to the user, remove it on session end

The agent forwarding socket's temp directory was left root-owned and
chmod 0755, letting every local user reach other users' agent sockets.
Chown the directory to the session user and keep it 0700 (the socket is
already 0600 and chowned first), like sshd's agent forwarding, and
remove the directory when the session ends instead of only closing the
listener.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: pin rejection-banner content to policy-derived facts

A policy rejection names the requested sshUser: that name is the
client's own request and reflects only tailnet policy (the client's
own ACL view), never a local-host fact, so naming it leaks nothing.
What a client-visible rejection must never depend on is server-side
local-user information: local-user lookup failures send one fixed
message for every failure cause, with the underlying error logged
server-side only, so the client cannot tell "no such local user"
from any other lookup failure and no banner is a
username-existence oracle.

Pin both properties in TestSSHAuthFlow: the user-mismatch cases,
including a rule whose "=" mapping forces a local lookup of a user
that does not exist, all name the requested user identically, and an
accept rule whose mapped local user fails lookup gets the fixed
lookup-failure banner.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: write private host keys with 0600 permissions

Private host keys are only ever read by tailscaled itself; writing them
0700 needlessly allows group/other to walk into the key directory.
Use 0600, and pin it in TestSSHKeyGen.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: treat numerically-zero uids as root in isRootUser

An NSS uid like "00" passed the string != "0" check but parses to 0 in
the incubator, so a session could bypass non-root checks and run as
root. Compare the uid numerically instead; non-numeric uids keep the
previous behavior.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: extend dangerous env var denylist, re-check child-side

GCONV_PATH, LOCPATH, NLSPATH, HOSTALIASES and RES_OPTIONS can make
privileged processes (root su/login environments built from forwarded
vars) load attacker-controlled files or redirect resolver lookups; add
them to the isDangerousEnvVar denylist, and apply the same check in the
incubator child when it re-filters the inherited forwarded-env payload
(old parents may not have filtered them).

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: make acceptEnv pattern matching linear time

matchAcceptEnvPattern recursively retried each '*' suffix, which is
exponential in the number of '*'s in an acceptEnv pattern (2.7s observed
on a 400-byte crafted variable name). Replace it with an iterative
matcher that only backtracks to the most recent '*', preserving the
exact OpenSSH-style glob semantics. Cross-check it against a naive
backtracking reference over random inputs, and pin the crafted
backtracking case as a timing regression test.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>

ssh/tailssh: record the raw client command in session recordings

The CastHeader recorded a shell-parsed reconstruction of the session
command, but the command is passed to the user's shell verbatim, and the
shell lexer silently drops unbalanced quotes. A spoofed command could
therefore make the recording differ from what the shell actually ran.
Record ss.RawCommand() instead.

Updates tailscale/corp#50380

Signed-off-by: James Tucker <james@tailscale.com>
